sections.title: Snapshot
sections.content: Daily GitHub Trending snapshot captured 2026-10-07 00:28 UTC. Date range: 2026-10-07 through 2026-10-07. Ranking by displayed daily star gains.

sections.title: Headline
sections.content: Agent-centric developer tools lead today's snapshot: REA's agent-assisted reverse engineering tops the daily gain list, alongside natural-language app testing, coding-agent skills, persistent agent memory, and CAD workflows. A few non-agent standouts—PS5 executable porting, a self-hosted fitness tracker, and DeepSeek's GPU kernels—show the list is not exclusively AI tooling.

sections.title: morluto/rea
sections.description: Reverse engineer anything with agents, from app behavior down to native binaries.
sections.why_notable: It leads the captured daily list; its README describes a local analysis workflow spanning native binaries, JavaScript/Electron apps, .NET assemblies, and websites, with evidence and limitations attached to results.

sections.title: tester-army/e2e
sections.description: Next generation e2e testing framework for web and mobile apps.
sections.why_notable: Strongest testing signal; the README says agent actions can be checked by ordinary assertions and replayed without repeated model calls until the app changes.

sections.title: DuarteSantos8/openGym
sections.description: Self-hosted gym & body-weight tracker — plan routines, log workouts (supersets, warm-ups, cardio), see which muscles are trained, fatigued or detrained, import from FitNotes/Strong/Hevy, passkey login. Your data, your server.
sections.why_notable: The leading personal-use app in this snapshot, with workout logging, imports, and passkey login described in its GitHub listing.

sections.title: boykopovar/AnyPS5
sections.description: Tool for automatic PS5 executables porting to Linux and Windows
sections.why_notable: A platform-compatibility project with nearly a thousand daily stars, standing out from the agent-heavy developer-tool cluster.

sections.title: mattpocock/skills
sections.description: Skills for Real Engineers. Straight from my .agents directory.
sections.why_notable: High absolute daily growth on an already large repo; its README emphasizes small, editable, model-agnostic agent skills rather than a single end-to-end process framework.

sections.title: msitarzewski/agency-agents
sections.description: A complete AI agency at your fingertips - From frontend wizards to Reddit community ninjas, from whimsy injectors to reality checkers. Each agent is a specialized expert with personality, processes, and proven deliverables.
sections.why_notable: Shows continued appetite for packaged, role-based agent workflows, from frontend work to community tasks.

sections.title: earthtojake/text-to-cad
sections.why_notable: Takes agent tooling into physical design: its README describes local generation of STEP/GLB/STL/3MF models, manufacturing checks, and drawing workflows.

sections.title: pbakaus/impeccable
sections.description: The design language that makes your AI harness better at design.
sections.why_notable: Design quality is being addressed as an agent-harness problem, extending the agent tooling theme beyond code generation.

sections.title: thedotmack/claude-mem
sections.description: Persistent Context Across Sessions for Every Agent – Captures everything your agent does during sessions, compresses it with AI, and injects relevant context back into future sessions. Works with Claude Code, OpenClaw, Codex, Gemini, Hermes, Copilot, OpenCode + More
sections.why_notable: Session memory is a distinct layer of agent infrastructure; the project says it captures, compresses, and retrieves relevant context across multiple agent environments.

sections.title: ayghri/i-have-adhd
sections.description: A skill to stop your coding agent from burying the answer. ADHD-friendly output.
sections.why_notable: A small, user-facing interaction preference packaged as an agent skill, rather than another agent runtime or model.

sections.title: cathrynlavery/diagram-design
sections.description: Editorial diagram design for Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot, Factory Droid, and Pi. 42 diagram types. Self-contained HTML + SVG. No shadows. No Mermaid slop.
sections.why_notable: Adds visual communication to the agent-tooling cluster, advertising 42 diagram types delivered as self-contained HTML and SVG.

sections.title: deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM
sections.description: DeepGEMM: clean and efficient BLAS kernel library on GPU
sections.why_notable: The systems-level counterpoint: its README describes runtime-compiled GPU kernels for dense and grouped GEMMs, with requirements centered on NVIDIA GPUs and CUDA.

sections.title: Trending Technologies and Themes
sections.content: Agent workflows are applied to testing, reverse engineering, CAD, and reusable task guidance. Agent infrastructure and UX projects focus on session memory, design quality, diagrams, and response format. Non-agent standouts include platform compatibility, self-hosted personal software, and GPU kernels. Languages: TypeScript (3), Shell (2), Python (2), JavaScript (2), C++ (1), CUDA (1), HTML (1).

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.content: The clearest signal is that coding agents are being surrounded by usable layers: persistent context, skills, design conventions, and workflows that test or manipulate real applications. Meanwhile, substantial growth for AnyPS5 and openGym—and continued visibility for DeepGEMM—shows that practical non-agent projects still break through. This is a snapshot of one day's GitHub Trending page, not a broad measure of all GitHub activity.

sections.title: Sources and Method
sections.content: Primary: https://github.com/trending?since=daily, captured 2026-10-07 at 00:28 UTC. Corroboration: GitHub REST API GET /repos/{owner}/{repo} and GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/commits/{default_branch} for each listed repository. Current README content reviewed for morluto/rea, tester-army/e2e, mattpocock/skills, earthtojake/text-to-cad, and deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM. Daily gains are the page's stars-today figures; no prior-window comparison was collected.
